text:
Microsoft's Recall feature, announced on May 20, 2024 [Source: ev-1], became a privacy scandal because security researchers demonstrated that the screenshots it captured were stored unencrypted in plaintext within a local SQLite database, contradicting Microsoft’s claims of encryption [Source: ev-1]. This insecure implementation allowed any process running as the user to access sensitive content visible on screen by default, including passwords and private messages [Source: ev-1]. The combination of this security failure and the feature’s initial design to record everything on screen (including health data) created a significant collision with privacy expectations [Source: ev-1].

In response to the controversy and inquiries from regulators such as the Irish Data Protection Commission and the UK Information Commissioner's Office, Microsoft delayed the release in June 2024 and subsequently changed the feature significantly [Source: ev-1]. Recall was relaunched as an opt-in feature that is off by default, rather than enabled automatically [Source: ev-1]. Additionally, accessing the timeline now requires Windows Hello authentication and presence detection, while incognito and DRM content are explicitly excluded from capture [Source: ev-1]. The revised version of the feature reached general availability on Copilot+ PCs in 2025 [Source: ev-1].
